name: Hassenua
title: Benjaminite Patriarch
summary: Hassenua (also spelled Hassenuah) was a man from the tribe of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies in Chronicles and Nehemiah. He is known as an ancestor of those who settled in Jerusalem after returning from the Babylonian exile. His descendants played a role in rebuilding Jerusalem and its community.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Benjamin's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Hassenua is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin as one of those who settled in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Descendants in Jerusalem After the Exile
keyEvents.description: Hassenua's descendants were among the Benjaminites who settled in Jerusalem after returning from Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Sallu, Son of Meshullam, Mentioned in Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: In Nehemiah's list of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Sallu is mentioned as a descendant of Hassenuah from the tribe of Benjamin.

keyEvents.title: Juda as second-in-command over the city
keyEvents.description: Juda, son of Hassenuah, was appointed second-in-command over Jerusalem under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: The Repopulation of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: As part of Nehemiah's reforms, selected families, including the descendants of Hassenuah, were chosen to settle in the holy city of Jerusalem.
